name: D1.8 Policies, standards, procedures and guidelines

paragraphes: On the first day of school, you get the school rules. They say the school must be a calm and safe place.
Lower down, you read: phones off during lessons. Next come the steps to get a phone back. Last, there is a tip: leave your phone at home.
These are four kinds of text. A company writes the same four for its security: policies, standards, procedures and guidelines.

decouverte.comme: The big rule says why: keep the school calm. The exact rule says what: phones off. The steps say how. The tip is just a suggestion.
decouverte.enVrai: In a company, the policy says WHY. The standard is an exact rule that says WHAT. The procedure is a list of steps that says HOW. The guideline is FYI, which means for your information. Nobody must follow it.

decouverte.question: The school writes: “During lessons, phones must be switched off.” What kind of text is this?
options: A big rule that says why
An exact rule that says what to do
A tip that anyone can ignore
decouverte.answer: An exact rule that says what to do
decouverte.explanation: It is exact and you must follow it, so it says WHAT. The big rule would be broad, like “keep the school calm”.

decouverte.texte: The policy: we protect our customers' data. The standard: a password has at least 12 characters. The procedure: the steps to make an account for a new worker. The guideline: use a password vault, a safe app that remembers your passwords.

decouverte.comme: Nobody rebuilds the foundations every year. But you can change the furniture often.
decouverte.enVrai: The policy is the foundation. It stays valid for years. Standards, procedures and guidelines are more exact, so they change more often.

cards.question: Official definition: “standards, procedures, and guidelines”
cards.answer: Standards, procedures, and guidelines are supporting elements that provide specific details to a complement an organization's policies.
cards.explanation: In simple words: the policy is the base. These three documents add the details that help it.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Develop, Document, and Implement Security Policy, Standards, Procedures, and Guidelines”. The manual has a small typing mistake (“to a complement”). Learn the sentence exactly like this.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “standards, procedures, and guidelines”?
options: Standards, procedures, and guidelines are separate elements that replace an organization's policies.
Standards, procedures, and guidelines are supporting elements that provide broad principles to an organization's policies.
Standards, procedures, and guidelines are supporting elements that provide specific details to a complement an organization's policies.
Standards, procedures, and guidelines are supporting elements that provide specific details to a complement an organization's technical controls.
options_why: It looks close, but these documents do not replace the policy. The key word is supporting.
Broad principles are the job of the policy. These three documents give specific details.
The details support the policies, not the technical controls.
cards.answer: Standards, procedures, and guidelines are supporting elements that provide specific details to a complement an organization's policies.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: supporting elements, specific details, policies.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “standards, procedures, and guidelines” from memory.
cards.answer: Standards, procedures, and guidelines are supporting elements that provide specific details to a complement an organization's policies.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: they support, they give specific details, and they help the policies.

cards.question: A company writes: “We protect our customers' data.” What kind of document is this?
options: A policy
A procedure
A guideline
A standard
options_why: A procedure lists steps. This sentence has no steps.
A guideline is only a tip. This sentence states a firm principle of the company.
A standard gives an exact requirement, like a number. This sentence is broad.
cards.answer: A policy
cards.explanation: It is a broad idea that lasts a long time, and it says why we act. That is a policy.

cards.question: Which document tells people HOW to do a task, step by step?
options: The policy
The standard
The guideline
The procedure
options_why: The policy says WHY. It does not give the steps.
The standard says WHAT is required. It does not give the steps.
The guideline is only a tip. It does not give exact steps.
cards.answer: The procedure
cards.explanation: HOW and WHO are the keywords of the procedure.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Develop, Document, and Implement Security Policy, Standards, Procedures, and Guidelines”. See figure 1.3.

cards.question: Which of these four documents is NOT mandatory?
options: The policy
The guideline
The standard
The procedure
options_why: A policy is a formal text that the company must follow.
A standard must be followed and enforced.
A procedure gives the steps that people follow to meet the policy and the standards.
cards.answer: The guideline
cards.explanation: A guideline is a recommendation. The other three documents say what people must do.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Develop, Document, and Implement Security Policy, Standards, Procedures, and Guidelines”.

cards.question: Which document is the BEST place for an exact rule such as “passwords have at least 14 characters”?
options: A policy
A standard
A procedure
A guideline
options_why: A policy stays broad. An exact number is too much detail for it.
A procedure lists steps. This rule is not a list of steps.
A guideline only suggests. This rule is required.
cards.answer: A standard
cards.explanation: An exact rule that can be checked is a standard.

cards.question: A manager writes the four documents on phone use at school. Which one should the manager write FIRST?
options: The standard
The procedure
The guideline
The policy
options_why: A standard supports a policy, so the policy must exist first.
Steps come after the rules they help to meet.
Tips support the policy. They do not come first.
cards.answer: The policy
cards.explanation: The policy is the foundation. The other three documents support it.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Develop, Document, and Implement Security Policy, Standards, Procedures, and Guidelines”.

cards.question: Which document is MOST likely to stay the same for many years?
options: The policy
The procedure
The standard
The guideline
options_why: Steps change when a tool changes.
A standard is exact, so it changes more often than a policy.
Tips and good practices change often.
cards.answer: The policy
cards.explanation: A policy is broad. It is less likely to change than the other documents.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Develop, Document, and Implement Security Policy, Standards, Procedures, and Guidelines”.

cards.question: In the manual's figure 1.3, which keyword goes with the standards?
options: WHY
HOW
WHAT
FYI
options_why: WHY goes with the policies.
HOW goes with the procedures.
FYI goes with the guidelines.
cards.answer: WHAT
cards.explanation: The standard says what is required, in an exact way.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Develop, Document, and Implement Security Policy, Standards, Procedures, and Guidelines”.

cards.question: A company has procedures and guidelines, but no policy. Which problem is MOST likely?
options: The steps will be right, but they will cost more money
The tips will turn into orders that workers must follow
There will be too many technical controls to manage
Nobody knows the main goal that the steps must serve
options_why: Cost is not the main problem. The steps have no goal to follow.
A guideline stays a recommendation. It does not become an order by itself.
The number of controls is not the problem. A missing goal is.
cards.answer: Nobody knows the main goal that the steps must serve
cards.explanation: The policy gives the goal. Without it, workers follow steps but do not know why.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT a job of a policy?
options: Setting the main principles of security
Listing the exact steps to restore a backup
Guiding decisions and actions in the company
Saying why security matters to the company
options_why: This is a real job of a policy.
This is a real job of a policy.
This is a real job of a policy.
cards.answer: Listing the exact steps to restore a backup
cards.explanation: Exact steps belong in a procedure. A policy sets principles.

cards.question: The manual says one part of a security program is the MOST essential. Which part is it?
options: Firewalls and other network tools
Encryption of all the data
Documents such as policies and procedures
Complex access control tools
options_why: They are important, but the manual says documents are more essential.
Encryption is important, but the manual puts documents first.
These tools help, but they follow the rules written in the documents.
cards.answer: Documents such as policies and procedures
cards.explanation: Technical controls are very important. But the manual says that policies, standards, procedures and guidelines are the most essential part.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Develop, Document, and Implement Security Policy, Standards, Procedures, and Guidelines”.

cards.question: Which keyword goes with each document: policy, standard, procedure, guideline?
cards.answer: Policy: WHY and WHEN. Standard: WHAT. Procedure: HOW and WHO. Guideline: FYI (for your information).
cards.explanation: One keyword for each document: why, what, how, for your information.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Develop, Document, and Implement Security Policy, Standards, Procedures, and Guidelines”. See figure 1.3.

cards.question: Why does a company not put everything in one big document?
cards.answer: The documents do not last the same time. The policy stays stable for years. The other three are exact, so they change more often.
cards.explanation: A broad, stable text should not be rewritten each time a tool changes.

cards.question: What happens if a company has procedures but no policy?
cards.answer: Workers follow steps but do not know why. In a new situation, nobody knows what to decide.
cards.explanation: Steps with no goal stop helping as soon as the situation changes.

cards.question: On the theme “phones at school”, give one example of each of the four documents.
cards.answer: Policy: the school stays calm. Standard: phones are off in class. Procedure: the steps to get a phone back. Guideline: leave your phone at home.
cards.explanation: Each example answers a different question: why, what, how, FYI.

decouverte.titre: The big rule of the school
paragraphes: At school, one rule says: “Everyone respects people and equipment.” It does not say how, and it does not name each object.
But every exact rule comes from it. And it stays the same from one year to the next.
In a company, a text like this is called a policy.

decouverte.comme: Nobody rebuilds the foundations every year. They hold up the house, even if you change the furniture.
decouverte.enVrai: A security policy is broad and stable. It often lasts for years. People review it from time to time to keep it up to date, but it hardly changes.

decouverte.question: Which of these sentences looks like a security policy?
options: We protect our customers' data
Click Settings, then Security, then Turn on
A password must have at least 14 characters
decouverte.explanation: The second sentence gives steps, so it is a procedure. The third gives an exact number, so it is a standard. The first states a broad principle.

decouverte.titre: The usual policies of a company
decouverte.texte: A company often has many policies. The acceptable use policy says what workers may do with the computers. The access control policy says who can open what. The change management policy says how to change a system without breaking it. Others cover remote access (working from outside the office) and disaster recovery (getting back to work after a big problem).

decouverte.comme: At school, a rule can be for everybody, only for the canteen, or for one subject, like school trips.
decouverte.enVrai: A policy can be company-wide, system-specific, or issue-specific. Issue-specific means about one subject. An example is a policy on how to respond to an incident, which is an event that threatens security.

cards.question: Official definition: “policy”
cards.answer: A policy is a formal set of statements that establish a system of principles to guide decisions and actions.
cards.explanation: In simple words: a policy is a written set of main ideas. It helps people decide what to do.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Policies”. You will need to know this sentence word for word.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “policy”?
options: A policy is a formal set of statements that establish a system of principles to guide decisions and actions.
A policy is an informal set of statements that establish a system of principles to guide decisions and actions.
A policy is a formal set of statements that establish a system of exact steps to guide decisions and actions.
A policy is a formal set of statements that establish a system of principles to record decisions and actions.
options_why: The real word is formal. A policy is an official, written text.
Exact steps are the job of a procedure. A policy uses principles.
A policy guides decisions. It does not only record them.
cards.answer: A policy is a formal set of statements that establish a system of principles to guide decisions and actions.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: formal, principles, guide decisions and actions.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “policy” from memory.
cards.answer: A policy is a formal set of statements that establish a system of principles to guide decisions and actions.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: it is formal, it rests on principles, and it guides decisions and actions.

cards.question: Official definition: “security policy”
cards.answer: More specifically, a security policy is a set of statements that identifies the principles and rules that govern an organization's protection of information systems and data.
cards.explanation: In simple words: a security policy is a set of main ideas and rules. They say how the company protects its systems and data.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “security policy”?
options: More specifically, a security policy is a set of statements that identifies the principles and rules that govern an organization's protection of information systems and data.
More specifically, a security policy is a set of statements that identifies the principles and rules that govern an organization's use of information systems and data.
More specifically, a security policy is a set of statements that identifies the steps and tools that govern an organization's protection of information systems and data.
More specifically, a security policy is a set of statements that identifies the principles and rules that govern an organization's protection of information systems only.
options_why: The real word is protection. A rule about use belongs to the acceptable use policy.
Steps belong to procedures and tools are technical. A policy sets principles and rules.
The word only is added. The real sentence covers systems and data.
cards.answer: More specifically, a security policy is a set of statements that identifies the principles and rules that govern an organization's protection of information systems and data.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: principles and rules, protection, information systems and data.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “security policy” from memory.
cards.answer: More specifically, a security policy is a set of statements that identifies the principles and rules that govern an organization's protection of information systems and data.
cards.explanation: Three parts: a set of statements, principles and rules, and the protection of systems and data.

cards.question: Official definition: the three sizes of a policy
cards.answer: Policies can be company-wide, system-specific, or issue-specific (e.g., an incident response policy).
cards.explanation: In simple words: a policy can cover the whole company, one system, or one subject.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about the three sizes of a policy from memory.
cards.answer: Policies can be company-wide, system-specific, or issue-specific (e.g., an incident response policy).
cards.explanation: Three sizes: the whole company, one system, one subject.

cards.question: Official definition: the role of policies
cards.answer: Policies set the foundation for your organization's security program and are typically written to be broad enough to be applicable and relevant for many years.
cards.explanation: In simple words: the policy is the base of the security program. It is broad, so it stays useful for many years.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Policies”. The manual compares the policy to the foundation of a building.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about the role of policies from memory.
cards.answer: Policies set the foundation for your organization's security program and are typically written to be broad enough to be applicable and relevant for many years.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the foundation of the program, broad enough to be useful, and lasting many years.

cards.question: Which description fits a policy BEST?
options: An exact list of steps for one task
A tip that workers may ignore
A broad text of principles that lasts for years
An exact number that is checked on each computer
options_why: That is a procedure. A policy does not give steps.
That is a guideline. A policy is formal.
That is a standard. A policy stays broad.
cards.answer: A broad text of principles that lasts for years
cards.explanation: A policy sets principles. It is written to stay useful for a long time.

cards.question: A company writes one policy that all workers and all departments must follow. What is its scope?
options: System-specific
Company-wide
Issue-specific
Device-specific
options_why: System-specific means it is for one system only.
Issue-specific means it is about one subject only.
The manual does not name this scope. It names company-wide, system-specific and issue-specific.
cards.answer: Company-wide
cards.explanation: A policy for the whole company is company-wide.

cards.question: Which of these is an issue-specific policy?
options: A policy for every office in the company
A policy that all departments must follow
A policy for the payroll system only
A policy on how to respond to incidents
options_why: That covers the whole company, so it is company-wide.
That is also company-wide.
That covers one system, so it is system-specific.
cards.answer: A policy on how to respond to incidents
cards.explanation: Issue-specific means about one subject. Responding to incidents is one subject.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Policies”. The manual gives the incident response policy as its example.

cards.question: Which policy says what workers may do with the company computers?
options: The access control policy
The change management policy
The acceptable use policy
The disaster recovery policy
options_why: This policy says who can open what, not what workers may do.
This policy says how to change systems safely.
This policy is about getting back to work after a big problem.
cards.answer: The acceptable use policy
cards.explanation: Acceptable use means the use that the company accepts.

cards.question: A manager wants to rewrite the access policy each month to follow new tools. What is the BEST advice?
options: Keep it broad and put the tool details in other documents
Rewrite it each month, since more changes mean more safety
Delete the policy and keep only guidelines
Add the name of each new tool to the policy
options_why: Changing often does not protect better. It creates confusion.
Guidelines are optional. The company still needs a formal base.
Tool names make the policy old fast. Details belong in standards and procedures.
cards.answer: Keep it broad and put the tool details in other documents
cards.explanation: A broad policy stays valid for years. The details change, so they go in other documents.

cards.question: A new security manager finds a policy that is ten years old. Nobody has read it since. What is the BEST action?
options: Leave it as it is, because policies never change
Throw it away and start with procedures
Replace it with a list of tips
Review it and update it where needed
options_why: The manual says policies should be reviewed and updated when needed.
Procedures need a policy to give them a goal.
Tips are optional. A policy must stay formal.
cards.answer: Review it and update it where needed
cards.explanation: A policy lasts a long time, but it must be reviewed from time to time and updated when needed.

cards.question: Which sentence is NOT a good policy statement?
options: The company protects the data of its customers
Passwords must have at least 14 characters
Only people who need access can use the systems
The company obeys the laws that apply to it
options_why: This is a broad principle, so it fits a policy.
This is a broad principle, so it fits a policy.
This is a broad principle, so it fits a policy.
cards.answer: Passwords must have at least 14 characters
cards.explanation: An exact number is too detailed for a policy. It belongs in a standard.

cards.question: A company lets workers log in from home. Which policy covers this?
options: The acceptable use policy
The remote access policy
The change management policy
The disaster recovery policy
options_why: This one says what workers may do with computers, not how they connect from outside.
This one is about changing systems safely.
This one is about getting back to work after a big problem.
cards.answer: The remote access policy
cards.explanation: Remote access means reaching the company systems from outside the office.

cards.question: Which statement about policies is NOT correct?
options: A policy is written to stay useful for many years
A policy should be reviewed from time to time
A policy can be about one subject only
A policy lists the exact settings of each computer
options_why: This is correct. Policies are broad enough to last.
This is correct. The manual says to review and update it when needed.
This is correct. That is an issue-specific policy.
cards.answer: A policy lists the exact settings of each computer
cards.explanation: Exact settings belong in standards and baselines. A policy stays broad.

cards.question: Why does the manual compare a policy to the foundation of a building?
options: It is the stable base that the other documents rest on
It is the longest and most detailed document
It must be rewritten every year
Only managers are allowed to read it
options_why: A policy is broad, not detailed.
A foundation does not change often. A policy is made to last.
The comparison is about being a stable base, not about secrecy.
cards.answer: It is the stable base that the other documents rest on
cards.explanation: A foundation holds the building for many years. A policy holds the security program in the same way.

cards.question: Name three examples of common security policies.
cards.answer: Acceptable use, access control and change management. Remote access and disaster recovery are also examples.
cards.explanation: Each policy covers one subject: use, access, change, remote work, disaster.

cards.question: Why do we write policies broad, not very exact?
cards.answer: So they stay valid for years, even when tools change. Exact details go in standards and procedures.
cards.explanation: An exact text gets old fast. A broad principle lasts.

cards.question: What is an issue-specific policy? Give an example.
cards.answer: A policy about one subject only. An example is a policy on how to respond to an incident.
cards.explanation: Issue means subject.

cards.question: Write one policy sentence about protecting customer data. Keep it broad.
cards.answer: For example: “We protect our customers' data from unauthorized access.”
cards.explanation: No number and no step: only a principle that can last for years.

paragraphes: The school rules say the school must stay calm. But they do not say exactly what you must do.
Then the teacher adds: “During lessons, phones are off and in your bag.” Now everyone knows what to do.
In a company, an exact rule like this is called a standard.

decouverte.titre: The exact rule in the lab
decouverte.comme: The rules say: “Be safe in the lab.” The exact rule says: “Wear goggles.” You follow it or you do not.
decouverte.enVrai: A standard is an exact rule that supports a policy. It says WHAT to do: a length, a setting or an allowed product. People must follow it, and the company checks it.

decouverte.question: Which of these sentences is a standard?
options: We protect our workers' passwords
Passwords have at least 14 characters
Remember to change your password sometimes
decouverte.explanation: The first states a principle, so it is a policy. The third is only a tip. Only the second is exact and required.

decouverte.titre: The standards of the US government
decouverte.texte: In the United States, an institute called NIST writes standards named FIPS. They are made for government agencies. FIPS 140-2 sets the security rules for cryptographic modules, the parts that lock data with a secret code. It says which devices are allowed and which are not.

decouverte.titre: When a standard becomes a must
decouverte.comme: You sign a rental contract: “Switch off the heating at night.” You must obey, because you signed.
decouverte.enVrai: A standard can be mandatory because of a contract or a law. Then the company has no choice. It must follow it.

cards.question: Official definition: “standards”
cards.answer: Standards are specific and granular requirements that give direction to support broader, higher-level policies.
cards.explanation: In simple words: a standard is an exact and detailed rule. It helps a broad policy work in real life. Granular means very detailed.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Standards”. You will need to know this sentence word for word.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “standards”?
options: Standards are broad and flexible suggestions that give direction to support specific, lower-level procedures.
Standards are specific and granular requirements that give direction to replace broader, higher-level policies.
Standards are specific and granular requirements that give direction to support broader, higher-level policies.
Standards are specific and granular requirements that give direction to support narrower, lower-level procedures.
options_why: This sounds like a guideline. A standard is a requirement, not a suggestion.
A standard supports a policy. It never replaces it.
Standards support the broader, higher-level policies, not the procedures.
cards.answer: Standards are specific and granular requirements that give direction to support broader, higher-level policies.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: specific and granular requirements, support, higher-level policies.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “standards” from memory.
cards.answer: Standards are specific and granular requirements that give direction to support broader, higher-level policies.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: exact requirements, they give direction, and they support broader policies.

cards.question: Official definition: “mandatory standards”
cards.answer: Standards may be mandatory for a given organization, if mandated by contract or law.
cards.explanation: In simple words: a standard can become a must for a company. A contract or a law can make it so.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “mandatory standards”?
options: Standards are always mandatory for every organization, whether or not a contract or law says so.
Standards may be mandatory for a given organization, if mandated by policy alone.
Standards may be mandatory for a given organization, if requested by a customer or a worker.
Standards may be mandatory for a given organization, if mandated by contract or law.
options_why: This is too extreme. The real sentence says may be mandatory, if a contract or a law requires it.
The manual names two sources: contract or law.
A request is not enough. A contract or a law is needed.
cards.answer: Standards may be mandatory for a given organization, if mandated by contract or law.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: may be mandatory, contract or law.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about “mandatory standards” from memory.
cards.answer: Standards may be mandatory for a given organization, if mandated by contract or law.
cards.explanation: Three parts: may be mandatory, for a given organization, and only by contract or law.

cards.question: Official definition: what standards establish
cards.answer: Standards establish specific behavior and actions that must be followed and enforced to satisfy policies.
cards.explanation: In simple words: a standard sets exact actions. People must follow them, and the company checks them.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about what standards establish from memory.
cards.answer: Standards establish specific behavior and actions that must be followed and enforced to satisfy policies.
cards.explanation: Three parts: exact actions, followed and enforced, to satisfy the policies.

cards.question: Official definition: “FIPS”
cards.answer: The Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS), for example, are publicly announced standards that were developed by NIST to establish various security requirements for U.S. government agencies; FIPS 140-2, for example, is a standard that establishes security requirements for cryptographic modules.
cards.explanation: In simple words: FIPS are public standards from NIST for US government agencies. FIPS 140-2 is about cryptographic modules, the parts that lock data with a secret code.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Standards”. The manual adds that FIPS 140-2 says which encryption devices are allowed or not in US government systems.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about “FIPS” from memory.
cards.answer: The Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS), for example, are publicly announced standards that were developed by NIST to establish various security requirements for U.S. government agencies; FIPS 140-2, for example, is a standard that establishes security requirements for cryptographic modules.
cards.explanation: Three landmarks: public standards, made by NIST, for government agencies. FIPS 140-2 is about cryptographic modules.

cards.question: A rule says: “Computers lock after 5 minutes without use.” What kind of document is this?
options: A policy
A standard
A procedure
A guideline
options_why: A policy would be broad, like “we protect our computers”.
A procedure would list steps in order.
A guideline would only suggest it. This rule is required.
cards.answer: A standard
cards.explanation: An exact time that can be checked is a requirement. That is a standard.

cards.question: Which words describe a standard BEST?
options: Broad and lasting
Flexible and optional
Exact and required
Step by step
options_why: That describes a policy.
That describes a guideline.
That describes a procedure.
cards.answer: Exact and required
cards.explanation: A standard is a specific and granular requirement.

cards.question: FIPS 140-2 sets security requirements for which of these?
options: Cryptographic modules
Password length
Backup schedules
Email filtering
options_why: Password length is a common standard, but it is not FIPS 140-2.
Backups are not the topic of FIPS 140-2.
Email is not the topic of FIPS 140-2.
cards.answer: Cryptographic modules
cards.explanation: Cryptographic modules are the parts that lock data with a secret code.

cards.question: A shop signs a contract with its bank. The contract says the shop must lock card data with one exact method. What is the BEST description of this rule for the shop?
options: A mandatory standard
An optional guideline
A broad policy
A procedure with steps
options_why: A guideline is followed freely. Here the contract forces the rule.
The rule is exact, not broad.
The rule says what to do, not the steps to follow.
cards.answer: A mandatory standard
cards.explanation: An exact requirement that a contract makes mandatory is a mandatory standard.

cards.question: Which of these sentences is a standard and NOT a policy?
options: The company protects its systems from attackers
The company obeys the laws that apply to it
Computers lock after 5 minutes without use
Data is kept safe at all times
options_why: This is a broad principle, so it is a policy.
This is a broad principle, so it is a policy.
This is a broad principle, so it is a policy.
cards.answer: Computers lock after 5 minutes without use
cards.explanation: A time that can be checked is a standard. Broad statements are policies.

cards.question: Which statement about standards is MOST accurate?
options: They are tips that workers may follow or skip
They must be followed and enforced
They replace the policy when it gets old
They are written only for government agencies
options_why: That describes a guideline.
A standard supports the policy. It does not replace it.
FIPS are for government agencies, but standards are used by any company.
cards.answer: They must be followed and enforced
cards.explanation: Standards establish exact behavior that must be followed and enforced to satisfy policies.

cards.question: A contract with a bank makes a security standard mandatory. A worker says it is only advice. What is the BEST answer?
options: It is optional, because standards are only advice
It is optional until the policy is rewritten
It is mandatory only for the managers
It is mandatory, because the contract requires it
options_why: Advice is a guideline. A standard is a requirement.
The contract makes it mandatory. The policy does not need to change first.
A contract binds the organization, not only the managers.
cards.answer: It is mandatory, because the contract requires it
cards.explanation: A standard may be mandatory if a contract or a law says so.

cards.question: Which document turns the broad goal of a policy into exact requirements that can be checked?
options: A guideline
A second policy
A standard
A procedure
options_why: A guideline only suggests. It cannot be checked as a requirement.
Another policy would be broad too.
A procedure gives steps, not the requirements to check.
cards.answer: A standard
cards.explanation: A policy is broad and hard to check. A standard gives exact requirements.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT true about a standard?
options: It is a flexible suggestion that workers may ignore
It is specific and detailed
It supports a broader policy
It can be mandatory because of a contract
options_why: This is true. A standard is specific and granular.
This is true. A standard supports higher-level policies.
This is true. A contract or a law can make it mandatory.
cards.answer: It is a flexible suggestion that workers may ignore
cards.explanation: A flexible suggestion is a guideline, not a standard.

cards.question: A policy says: “We protect worker accounts.” Which standard BEST supports it?
options: Workers should think of strong passwords
Accounts are important to the company
Open the tool, click New, then fill in the form
Each account has a password of at least 14 characters
options_why: This is only a tip, so it is not a standard.
This is a statement of value, not a requirement.
These are steps, so this is a procedure.
cards.answer: Each account has a password of at least 14 characters
cards.explanation: A standard is exact and can be checked. A number of characters can be checked.

cards.question: What does FIPS stand for, and who writes these standards?
cards.answer: Federal Information Processing Standards. NIST writes them for US government agencies.
cards.explanation: Federal means the US government.

cards.question: Which FIPS standard sets the security requirements for cryptographic modules?
cards.answer: FIPS 140-2.
cards.explanation: Link the number 140-2 with locking data with a secret code.

cards.question: Why does a policy need standards?
cards.answer: A policy is broad and hard to check. A standard gives exact requirements that can be checked.
cards.explanation: Without standards, everyone would read the policy in their own way.

cards.question: Write a standard that supports this policy: “We protect worker accounts.”
cards.answer: For example: “Each account has a password of at least 14 characters.”
cards.explanation: A standard is exact: a number that can be checked.

paragraphes: The school gets thirty new computers. The technician sets up each one in the same way. The antivirus, a tool that finds bad software, is on. The updates are automatic.
A computer without these settings is not accepted. You can add more, but you can never remove them.
This common minimum level is called a baseline.

decouverte.comme: For a day in the woods, everyone must carry water, a coat and a torch. You can carry more, but never less.
decouverte.enVrai: A baseline is the minimum level of security for a system, a network or a device. You can do better, but never worse. A company often keeps one baseline for each operating system, the main software of a computer.

decouverte.question: A company uses three different operating systems. How many baselines can it keep?
options: Only one for everything
One for each operating system
None: it decides each time
decouverte.explanation: Each system has its own settings. The manual gives this example: one baseline for each operating system.

decouverte.texte: Ahmed sets up a new server, a computer that serves other computers. Its baseline lists: firewall on, useless accounts removed, updates installed. A firewall is a guard between the computer and the internet. These are the minimum settings to meet the company's standards.

decouverte.comme: The woods list says: “No more than 8 kilos.” You pick your things inside this limit.
decouverte.enVrai: Scoping guidance says how far you can move away from the baseline. Tailoring means picking the security controls that reach the baseline inside these limits. A control is a tool or a rule that protects.

cards.question: Official definition: “baselines”
cards.answer: Baselines are related to standards and establish a minimum level of a security for a system, network, or device.
cards.explanation: In simple words: a baseline is the lowest level of security that is allowed. It covers a system, a network or a device.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Standards”. The manual has a small typing mistake (“of a security”). Learn the sentence exactly like this.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “baselines”?
options: Baselines are related to guidelines and establish a minimum level of a security for a system, network, or device.
Baselines are related to standards and establish a minimum level of a security for a system, network, or device.
Baselines are related to standards and establish a maximum level of a security for a system, network, or device.
Baselines are related to standards and establish a minimum level of a security for a person, team, or department.
options_why: Baselines are related to standards. A guideline is only a tip.
A baseline is a minimum. You can do better, never worse.
A baseline covers technology: a system, a network or a device.
cards.answer: Baselines are related to standards and establish a minimum level of a security for a system, network, or device.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: related to standards, minimum level, system, network, or device.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “baselines” from memory.
cards.answer: Baselines are related to standards and establish a minimum level of a security for a system, network, or device.
cards.explanation: Three parts: related to standards, a minimum level, and a system, network or device.

cards.question: Official definition: “security baselines”
cards.answer: As a subset of baselines, security baselines express the minimum set of security controls necessary to safeguard the CIA and other security properties for a particular configuration.
cards.explanation: In simple words: a security baseline is the smallest list of controls that protects the CIA for one setup. CIA means confidentiality, integrity and availability.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “security baselines”?
options: As a subset of baselines, security baselines express the maximum set of security controls necessary to safeguard the CIA and other security properties for a particular configuration.
As a subset of baselines, security baselines express the minimum set of security controls necessary to safeguard the CIA and other security properties for a particular configuration.
As a subset of baselines, security baselines express the minimum set of security controls necessary to safeguard the CIA and other security properties for every configuration.
As a superset of baselines, security baselines express the minimum set of security controls necessary to safeguard the CIA and other security properties for a particular configuration.
options_why: A baseline is the minimum set, not the maximum.
A security baseline fits one particular configuration, not every one.
Security baselines are a subset, which means one smaller part of baselines. A superset would be a bigger group.
cards.answer: As a subset of baselines, security baselines express the minimum set of security controls necessary to safeguard the CIA and other security properties for a particular configuration.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: subset, minimum set of security controls, safeguard the CIA, particular configuration.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “security baselines” from memory.
cards.answer: As a subset of baselines, security baselines express the minimum set of security controls necessary to safeguard the CIA and other security properties for a particular configuration.
cards.explanation: Three parts: a subset of baselines, the minimum set of controls, and the CIA for one particular configuration.

cards.question: Official definition: “scoping guidance”
cards.answer: Scoping guidance is often published as part of a baseline, defining the range of deviation from the baseline that is acceptable for a particular baseline.
cards.explanation: In simple words: scoping guidance tells you how far you may move away from the baseline.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Standards”. The manual sends you to chapter 2 (Asset Security) for more.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about “scoping guidance” from memory.
cards.answer: Scoping guidance is often published as part of a baseline, defining the range of deviation from the baseline that is acceptable for a particular baseline.
cards.explanation: Three parts: published with the baseline, the range of deviation, and what is acceptable.

cards.question: Official definition: “tailoring”
cards.answer: Once scoping guidance has been established, then tailoring is performed to apply a particular set of controls to achieve the baseline within the scoping guidance.
cards.explanation: In simple words: tailoring means choosing the controls that reach the baseline. You stay inside the limits of the scoping guidance.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Standards”. A tailor makes clothes to fit one person. Tailoring here means making the controls fit one setup.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about “tailoring” from memory.
cards.answer: Once scoping guidance has been established, then tailoring is performed to apply a particular set of controls to achieve the baseline within the scoping guidance.
cards.explanation: Three parts: scoping guidance first, then tailoring, to reach the baseline inside the limits.

cards.question: A company has a baseline for its computers. A technician sets one up without the firewall that the baseline requires. What is the situation?
options: The firewall was only a tip, so nothing is wrong
The firewall can wait, because baselines are goals for later
The baseline only applies to servers, not to computers
A minimum is missing, so the computer does not comply
options_why: A baseline sets a minimum to respect. It is not a tip.
The minimum must be in place, not added later.
A baseline covers a system, a network or a device.
cards.answer: A minimum is missing, so the computer does not comply
cards.explanation: A baseline is a minimum level. Below it, the setup does not meet the company's standards.

cards.question: Which words describe a baseline BEST?
options: A minimum level
A maximum level
A flexible tip
A list of steps
options_why: You can do better than a baseline, so it is not a maximum.
That describes a guideline.
That describes a procedure.
cards.answer: A minimum level
cards.explanation: A baseline is the lowest level of security that is allowed.

cards.question: A company uses three operating systems. What does the manual say the company may keep?
options: One baseline for the whole company only
No baseline, only policies
One baseline for each operating system
One baseline for each worker
options_why: The manual gives one baseline per operating system as an example.
Policies are broad. A baseline lists the exact settings.
A baseline covers systems, networks and devices, not people.
cards.answer: One baseline for each operating system
cards.explanation: Each system has its own settings, so each one can have its own baseline.

cards.question: A team picks the controls that reach the baseline, inside the allowed limits. What is this called?
options: Scoping guidance
A security baseline
A guideline
Tailoring
options_why: Scoping guidance sets the limits. It does not pick the controls.
A security baseline is the minimum list of controls, not the act of choosing them.
A guideline is a recommendation.
cards.answer: Tailoring
cards.explanation: First the scoping guidance sets the limits. Then tailoring picks the controls inside them.

cards.question: A document says how far a system may move away from the baseline. What is it?
options: Tailoring
Scoping guidance
A procedure
A policy
options_why: Tailoring is the act of picking controls. It does not set the range.
A procedure lists steps.
A policy is broad and does not set the range for one baseline.
cards.answer: Scoping guidance
cards.explanation: Scoping guidance defines the acceptable range of deviation from the baseline.

cards.question: Which statement about baselines is NOT correct?
options: A baseline sets a minimum level of security
A company may keep one baseline per operating system
A baseline sets the maximum security a system may have
A baseline lists settings, applications and configurations
options_why: This is correct. A baseline is a minimum.
This is correct. It is the manual's example.
This is correct. They must be in place to meet the standards.
cards.answer: A baseline sets the maximum security a system may have
cards.explanation: A baseline is a minimum. You can do better, but never worse.

cards.question: A technician adds extra security above the baseline on one server. Which comment is MOST accurate?
options: This is fine, because a baseline is a minimum
This is not allowed, because a baseline is an exact target
This is allowed only after the policy is rewritten
This is allowed only for servers on the internet
options_why: A baseline is a floor, not an exact target.
The policy does not need to change to do more than the minimum.
The minimum applies to all, and doing more is not limited to them.
cards.answer: This is fine, because a baseline is a minimum
cards.explanation: A baseline sets the lowest level. Doing better is fine. Doing worse is not.

cards.question: A team must change one setting of the baseline for special laptops. What should the team check FIRST?
options: The scoping guidance, to see how far it may deviate
A guideline that says the change is a good idea
Whether other companies made the same change
Whether the change saves money
options_why: A guideline is only advice. The range of deviation is set by the scoping guidance.
What other companies do does not set your limit.
Cost is not the first check. The allowed range is.
cards.answer: The scoping guidance, to see how far it may deviate
cards.explanation: The scoping guidance defines the acceptable range of deviation from the baseline.

cards.question: Which of these is the BEST example of a baseline setting for a new server?
options: A tip to use a password vault
The steps to restore a backup
Firewall on and updates installed
The main goal of the security program
options_why: That is a guideline, so it is optional.
That is a procedure.
That is the job of a policy.
cards.answer: Firewall on and updates installed
cards.explanation: A baseline lists the minimum settings that must be in place.

cards.question: The manual says baselines are not named in the CBK, the official list of exam topics. What is the BEST way to treat them?
options: Skip them, because they are not named
Learn them and know where they fit
Learn them only after the exam
Treat them as policies
options_why: The manual says you should be familiar with baselines.
They help you to understand how the documents fit together.
A baseline is related to standards, not to policies.
cards.answer: Learn them and know where they fit
cards.explanation: The manual says you should be familiar with baselines and understand how they fit into the bigger picture.

cards.question: How many baselines can a company have?
cards.answer: Several. For example, one for each operating system that it uses.
cards.explanation: Each system has its own settings and applications.

cards.question: What is a baseline? Say it in your own words.
cards.answer: The lowest level of security that is allowed for a system, network or device. You can do more, never less.
cards.explanation: Think of what you must carry in the backpack.

cards.question: What does a security baseline protect?
cards.answer: The CIA (confidentiality, integrity and availability) and other security properties, for one particular configuration.
cards.explanation: It is the minimum list of controls for one setup.

cards.question: What three things does a baseline list, according to the manual?
cards.answer: The settings, applications and configurations that must be in place.
cards.explanation: They must be in place to meet the company's security standards.

paragraphes: Your family wants to make pancakes. The house rule says: “We cook cleanly and do not waste food.”
But your little brother does not know how to start. You give him the recipe: 1. mix, 2. let it rest, 3. cook.
This recipe, with steps one after the other, is called a procedure.

decouverte.comme: A recipe gives the steps in order. If you follow it, you get the result you want.
decouverte.enVrai: A procedure is a detailed guide, step by step, to reach a goal. It says HOW to do it, and also WHO does it. The image stops there: a bad pancake is harmless, but a bad security procedure can cost you data.

decouverte.question: Which of these is a procedure?
options: Backups are locked with a secret code
Step 1: plug in the disk. Step 2: start the tool. Step 3: pick the date
We protect our data
decouverte.answer: Step 1: plug in the disk. Step 2: start the tool. Step 3: pick the date
decouverte.explanation: The first is a requirement, so a standard. The third is a principle, so a policy. Only the second gives steps.

decouverte.titre: Making the account of a new worker
decouverte.texte: Every new worker needs an account. The procedure lists: 1. get the manager's request, 2. make the account, 3. give only the access that is needed, 4. write the action in the log, a written record. The steps are written in advance, so nobody forgets one.

Vulnerability scanning means checking for weak points. Backup and restore means saving data and getting it back. Account provisioning means making accounts for new workers. Patch management means installing the updates that fix problems.

cards.question: Official definition: “procedure”
cards.answer: A procedure is a detailed step-by-step guide to achieve a particular goal or requirement.
cards.explanation: In simple words: a procedure is a list of steps in order. If you follow it, you reach a goal.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Procedures”. You will need to know this sentence word for word.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “procedure”?
options: A procedure is a broad set of principles to achieve a particular goal or requirement.
A procedure is a detailed step-by-step guide to achieve a particular goal or recommendation.
A procedure is a flexible step-by-step suggestion to achieve a particular goal or requirement.
A procedure is a detailed step-by-step guide to achieve a particular goal or requirement.
options_why: Principles belong to a policy. A procedure gives detailed steps.
The real word is requirement. A procedure helps to meet a requirement.
A procedure is detailed. Flexible suggestions describe a guideline.
cards.answer: A procedure is a detailed step-by-step guide to achieve a particular goal or requirement.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: detailed, step-by-step guide, goal or requirement.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “procedure” from memory.
cards.answer: A procedure is a detailed step-by-step guide to achieve a particular goal or requirement.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: it is detailed, it goes step by step, and it reaches a goal or a requirement.

cards.question: Official definition: what procedures are for
cards.answer: Procedures tell you how to implement your policies and how to meet your standards and baselines.
cards.explanation: In simple words: procedures show how to apply the policies. They also show how to meet the standards and baselines.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official description of what procedures are for?
options: Procedures tell you why to implement your policies and why to meet your standards and baselines.
Procedures tell you how to implement your policies and how to replace your standards and baselines.
Procedures tell you how to implement your policies and how to meet your standards and baselines.
Procedures tell you how to write your policies and how to meet your standards and baselines.
options_why: Why is the job of the policy. A procedure tells you how.
Procedures help to meet standards and baselines. They do not replace them.
A procedure helps to implement a policy. It is not a way to write one.
cards.answer: Procedures tell you how to implement your policies and how to meet your standards and baselines.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: how, implement policies, meet standards and baselines.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about what procedures are for from memory.
cards.answer: Procedures tell you how to implement your policies and how to meet your standards and baselines.
cards.explanation: Two jobs: apply the policies, and meet the standards and baselines. The key word is how.

cards.question: A text says: “To restore a backup: open the tool, pick the date, click Restore.” What kind of document is it?
options: A procedure
A policy
A standard
A guideline
options_why: A policy sets principles. It does not list actions.
A standard says what is required, not the actions to take.
A guideline is a tip. This text gives exact steps.
cards.answer: A procedure
cards.explanation: Actions in order, to reach a goal: that is a procedure.

cards.question: In the manual's figure 1.3, which keywords go with procedures?
options: WHY and WHEN
WHAT
FYI
HOW and WHO
options_why: These go with the policies.
This goes with the standards.
This goes with the guidelines.
cards.answer: HOW and WHO
cards.explanation: A procedure says how to do a task, and who does it.

cards.question: Which of these is an example of a security procedure?
options: A password of 14 characters for each account
The steps to back up and restore data
We protect our data at all times
A tip to use a password vault
options_why: This is an exact requirement, so it is a standard.
This is a broad principle, so it is a policy.
This is a recommendation, so it is a guideline.
cards.answer: The steps to back up and restore data
cards.explanation: Backup and restore is one of the procedures named in the manual.

cards.question: A company wants everyone to restore a backup in the same way after a breakdown. Which document is the BEST choice?
options: A general policy
A step-by-step procedure
An optional guideline
A standard with numbers
options_why: A policy sets a principle. It does not say how to restore.
A guideline does not make sure that everyone does the same thing.
A standard says what is required, not the actions to take.
cards.answer: A step-by-step procedure
cards.explanation: We want exact actions in order. That is a procedure.

cards.question: A procedure for a new worker's account has four steps. Which step comes right AFTER the IT team makes the account?
options: Get the manager's request
Write the action in the log
Give full access to check that the account works
Give only the access that is needed
options_why: The request comes first, before the account exists.
The log comes last, after the access is set.
This breaks the idea of giving only the access that is needed.
cards.answer: Give only the access that is needed
cards.explanation: The order is: request, make the account, give only the needed access, write it in the log.

cards.question: A server breaks and a worker forgets an important step. What would have helped MOST?
options: A written procedure prepared in advance
A longer policy
A new guideline with tips
A stricter standard
options_why: A policy gives the goal, not the steps.
Tips are optional and do not give the exact order.
A standard says what is required. It does not list the actions.
cards.answer: A written procedure prepared in advance
cards.explanation: You write the procedure when all is well, for the day when things go wrong.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT a security procedure named in the manual?
options: Vulnerability scanning procedures
Account provisioning procedures
Writing the acceptable use policy
Patch management procedures
options_why: This one is named in the manual.
This one is named in the manual.
This one is named in the manual.
cards.answer: Writing the acceptable use policy
cards.explanation: The manual names vulnerability scanning, backup and restore, account provisioning and patch management.

cards.question: A CISSP must also check HR procedures (the people team) and transaction procedures. What must the CISSP make sure of?
options: That the IT team writes all of them
That they all become security policies
That they are ignored, since they are not about security
That they are safe, secure and compliant
options_why: The manual does not say who writes them.
They stay procedures. They only have to follow the policies.
The manual says a CISSP must make sure they are safe and compliant.
cards.answer: That they are safe, secure and compliant
cards.explanation: The manual says non-security procedures must also be safe, secure and compliant with the policies and standards.

cards.question: Which statement about procedures is MOST accurate?
options: They set the main goals of the company
They help to apply policies and meet standards
They are the same thing as policies
They replace the standards when these are old
options_why: That is the job of the policy.
A policy is broad. A procedure is detailed.
Procedures help to meet standards. They do not replace them.
cards.answer: They help to apply policies and meet standards
cards.explanation: Procedures tell you how to implement your policies and meet your standards and baselines.

cards.question: Which of these is a procedure and NOT a standard?
options: Computers must have the latest updates
All updates are installed within a set time
Step 1: back up the data. Step 2: install the update
Updates keep the company safe
options_why: This is an exact requirement, so it is a standard.
This is an exact requirement, so it is a standard.
This is a broad statement, so it is closer to a policy.
cards.answer: Step 1: back up the data. Step 2: install the update
cards.explanation: Steps in order are a procedure. A requirement is a standard.

cards.question: Name three examples of security procedures.
cards.answer: Backup and restore, account provisioning, vulnerability scanning or patch management.
cards.explanation: Each one is a task that is repeated, so it is better done with written steps.

cards.question: Which keywords go with procedures in the manual's figure?
cards.answer: HOW and WHO.
cards.explanation: How we do it, and who does it.

cards.question: Why write a procedure when the workers are skilled?
cards.answer: So everyone does the task in the same way, even a new worker or someone under stress. It stops forgotten steps and mistakes.
cards.explanation: A forgotten step can leave a door open.

cards.question: Write a three-step procedure to install a security update.
cards.answer: For example: 1. Back up the data. 2. Start the update. 3. Check that all works and write the action in the log.
cards.explanation: Steps in order, with a check at the end.

paragraphes: The maths teacher says: “If you find it hard, do the extra exercises.” Nobody forces you.
The school rules say: “Homework is a must.” If you skip it, you get a punishment.
The teacher's tip is a recommendation. In security, it is called a guideline.

decouverte.titre: An advised speed on the road
decouverte.comme: On some road signs, a speed is only advised. You can choose not to follow it. A speed limit is a must.
decouverte.enVrai: A guideline looks like a standard, but it recommends instead of forcing. It gives flexible suggestions to reach the goal of the policy.

decouverte.question: A document says: “It is recommended to protect your USB sticks.” What happens if a worker does not do it?
options: They break a mandatory standard
They do not follow a recommendation, which is not mandatory
They are punished at once
decouverte.answer: They do not follow a recommendation, which is not mandatory
decouverte.explanation: “Recommended” means suggested, not required. That is the difference with a standard. Later, a company can decide to make a guideline mandatory.

decouverte.texte: A framework is a ready-made set of good practices. ISO and NIST publish frameworks, and ITIL is a framework for running IT. Companies often use them as guidelines. Makers of products give default settings, the settings that come with the product. Each industry can also have its own guidelines. OWASP, an independent group, gives tips for writing safe software.

decouverte.titre: When a tip becomes a rule
decouverte.comme: The teacher advises you to learn the lesson. One day, the school rules require it. Now it is a rule.
decouverte.enVrai: A framework like ISO or NIST starts as a guideline. If the company has a compliance expectation, it can become a policy or a standard. Compliance means following the rules that apply to you.

cards.question: Official definition: “guideline”
cards.answer: A guideline is similar to a standard but is a recommendation rather than a mandatory requirement.
cards.explanation: In simple words: a guideline is like a standard, but it is only advice. Nobody must follow it.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Guidelines”. You will need to know this sentence word for word.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “guideline”?
options: A guideline is similar to a standard but is a recommendation rather than a mandatory requirement.
A guideline is similar to a policy but is a recommendation rather than a mandatory requirement.
A guideline is similar to a standard but is a mandatory requirement rather than a recommendation.
A guideline is similar to a procedure but is a recommendation rather than a mandatory requirement.
options_why: A guideline is like a standard, which is exact. A policy is broad.
The two key words are swapped. A guideline is a recommendation, not mandatory.
A guideline is like a standard. A procedure is a list of steps.
cards.answer: A guideline is similar to a standard but is a recommendation rather than a mandatory requirement.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: similar to a standard, recommendation, mandatory requirement.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “guideline” from memory.
cards.answer: A guideline is similar to a standard but is a recommendation rather than a mandatory requirement.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: close to a standard, a recommendation, and not mandatory.

cards.question: Official definition: the ISO, NIST and ITIL frameworks
cards.answer: The ISO/NIST/ITIL frameworks are often leveraged as guidelines; however, they may become policies or standards if the organization has a compliance expectation.
cards.explanation: In simple words: these frameworks are usually just guidelines. They can become mandatory if the company must follow them.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Guidelines”. ITIL is a framework for running IT (this detail is from outside the manual).

cards.question: Which sentence is the official description of the ISO, NIST and ITIL frameworks?
options: The ISO/NIST/ITIL frameworks are often leveraged as guidelines; however, they may become policies or standards if the organization has a compliance expectation.
The ISO/NIST/ITIL frameworks are always leveraged as policies; however, they may become guidelines if the organization has a compliance expectation.
The ISO/NIST/ITIL frameworks are often leveraged as guidelines; however, they may become procedures or baselines if the organization has a compliance expectation.
The ISO/NIST/ITIL frameworks are often leveraged as guidelines; however, they may become policies or standards if the organization has a budget expectation.
options_why: The order is swapped. They are guidelines first, and they may become policies or standards later.
They may become policies or standards, not procedures or baselines.
The reason is a compliance expectation, not a budget.
cards.answer: The ISO/NIST/ITIL frameworks are often leveraged as guidelines; however, they may become policies or standards if the organization has a compliance expectation.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: guidelines, may become policies or standards, compliance expectation.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about the ISO, NIST and ITIL frameworks from memory.
cards.answer: The ISO/NIST/ITIL frameworks are often leveraged as guidelines; however, they may become policies or standards if the organization has a compliance expectation.
cards.explanation: Three parts: often guidelines, may become policies or standards, and the reason is a compliance expectation.

cards.question: Official definition: what guidelines do
cards.answer: Guidelines refer to policy statements and offer flexible suggestions for meeting the intent of the policy or recommendations to implement the requirements in standards and baselines.
cards.explanation: In simple words: guidelines give flexible tips to reach the goal of a policy. They also help to apply standards and baselines.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about what guidelines do from memory.
cards.answer: Guidelines refer to policy statements and offer flexible suggestions for meeting the intent of the policy or recommendations to implement the requirements in standards and baselines.
cards.explanation: Three parts: they refer to policy statements, they offer flexible suggestions, and they help with standards and baselines.

cards.question: A document says: “It is recommended to use a password vault.” What kind of document is it?
options: A standard
A procedure
A guideline
A policy
options_why: A standard is a requirement. This sentence only recommends.
A procedure lists steps. This sentence gives no steps.
A policy sets a broad principle. This sentence is a tip.
cards.answer: A guideline
cards.explanation: The word recommended shows a guideline.

cards.question: What is the main difference between a standard and a guideline?
options: A standard is longer than a guideline
A standard is mandatory, a guideline is advised
A guideline is mandatory, a standard is advised
A standard is for managers, a guideline is for workers
options_why: Length is not the difference.
The two are swapped.
Both are for anyone who needs them.
cards.answer: A standard is mandatory, a guideline is advised
cards.explanation: A guideline is similar to a standard but is a recommendation, not a mandatory requirement.

cards.question: A company reads the NIST framework. No contract or law forces it to follow it. What is the framework for this company?
options: A law
A mandatory standard
An internal procedure
A source of guidelines
options_why: NIST publishes frameworks. It does not write laws for private companies.
It becomes mandatory only if the company has a compliance expectation.
A procedure is written by the company, with steps.
cards.answer: A source of guidelines
cards.explanation: With no compliance expectation, a framework stays a guideline.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT a source of guidelines named in the manual?
options: The default settings from a product maker
Frameworks such as ISO, NIST and ITIL
A signed contract with a bank
Tips from OWASP, an independent group
options_why: This one is named in the manual.
These are named in the manual.
This one is named in the manual.
cards.answer: A signed contract with a bank
cards.explanation: A contract can make a standard mandatory. It is not a source of guidelines.

cards.question: A law now requires a company to follow the ISO framework. What does the framework become?
options: A policy or a standard
A guideline with more pages
A procedure with steps
A tip for managers
options_why: A guideline is only a recommendation. A law makes it mandatory.
A framework is not a list of steps.
A tip is optional. A law is not.
cards.answer: A policy or a standard
cards.explanation: A framework may become a policy or a standard if the company has a compliance expectation.

cards.question: Which sentence is a guideline and NOT a standard?
options: Passwords have at least 14 characters
Screens lock after 5 minutes without use
Only approved devices may be plugged in
We suggest that you lock your screen when you leave
options_why: This is an exact requirement, so it is a standard.
This is an exact requirement, so it is a standard.
This is a requirement, so it is a standard.
cards.answer: We suggest that you lock your screen when you leave
cards.explanation: Words like suggest or recommend show a guideline. Words like must show a standard.

cards.question: A manager wants all workers to follow a rule on locking screens. Which document is the BEST choice?
options: A guideline
A standard
A procedure
A policy
options_why: A guideline is flexible. Workers may skip it.
A procedure lists steps, but it does not make the rule required.
A policy is too broad to give the exact rule.
cards.answer: A standard
cards.explanation: A standard is required, followed and enforced.

cards.question: A company has only guidelines, with no policy and no standard. What is the MOST likely result?
options: Workers must follow every tip
Nothing is mandatory, so workers may do as they like
The company is fully compliant
The guidelines turn into procedures
options_why: A guideline is a recommendation, so workers are free to skip it.
Compliance needs requirements. Tips alone do not give them.
A guideline does not become a procedure by itself.
cards.answer: Nothing is mandatory, so workers may do as they like
cards.explanation: Without a policy or a standard, nothing is required.

cards.question: Which document gives flexible suggestions to help meet the goal of a policy?
options: A baseline
A standard
A procedure
A guideline
options_why: A baseline sets a minimum level. It is not flexible.
A standard is a requirement.
A procedure gives exact steps.
cards.answer: A guideline
cards.explanation: Guidelines offer flexible suggestions for meeting the intent of the policy.

cards.question: Which statement about guidelines is NOT correct?
options: A guideline must be enforced like a standard
A guideline offers flexible suggestions
A guideline can come from a product maker
A guideline can become a policy or a standard
options_why: This is correct.
This is correct. Default settings are a source.
This is correct, if the company has a compliance expectation.
cards.answer: A guideline must be enforced like a standard
cards.explanation: A standard is enforced. A guideline is a recommendation.

cards.question: Name three sources of guidelines in the manual.
cards.answer: Frameworks such as ISO, NIST and ITIL; default settings from product makers; and groups such as OWASP. Guides for an industry also count.
cards.explanation: These sources give good ideas but do not force a company.

cards.question: What does FYI mean in the manual's figure?
cards.answer: “For your information”. It is a suggestion, not an order.
cards.explanation: FYI informs. It does not force.

cards.question: When can a framework like NIST become mandatory?
cards.answer: When the company has a compliance expectation, for example from a contract or a law. It then becomes a policy or a standard.
cards.explanation: What changes is the duty to follow it, not the content.

cards.question: Write a standard and a guideline on the same subject: passwords.
cards.answer: Standard: passwords have at least 14 characters. Guideline: use a password vault to remember your passwords.
cards.explanation: The standard is required and exact. The guideline helps without forcing.

concepts.name: Policy, standard, procedure, guideline: comparing them

paragraphes: The company Pizza Express was hacked. The addresses of its customers have leaked.
The boss wants to put things in order. The company needs a text of principles, exact rules, steps and a few tips.
For each need, the boss must pick the right document. You will learn to do this now.

decouverte.titre: School and company, side by side
decouverte.comme: School: “The school stays calm and safe” says why. “Phones off in class” says what. “To get a phone back: steps 1, 2, 3” says how. “Leave it at home” is a tip.
decouverte.enVrai: Company: “We protect our customers' data” is a policy. “Passwords have 14 characters” is a standard. “To make an account: steps 1, 2, 3” is a procedure. “Use a password vault” is a guideline.

decouverte.question: The boss wants everyone to know what to do, step by step, when a strange email arrives. Which document does the boss need?
options: A policy
A procedure
A guideline
decouverte.explanation: The boss wants steps to follow: the HOW. The policy gives the principle, and the guideline is optional.

decouverte.texte: Subject: backups. Policy: the company's data must be able to come back after a loss. Standard: a backup is made every night. Procedure: to restore, open the tool, pick the date, start. Guideline: keep a copy in another building.

cards.question: Pizza Express wants to explain, in a few broad sentences, why security matters. Which document should it write?
options: A standard
A procedure
A policy
A guideline
options_why: A standard gives exact requirements, not a general explanation.
A procedure gives steps, not a principle.
A guideline is optional. Here the company needs a clear direction.
cards.answer: A policy
cards.explanation: A broad principle that guides decisions is the job of a policy.

cards.question: Pizza Express wants every computer to have an up-to-date antivirus. Which document gives this exact requirement?
options: A policy
A guideline
A procedure
A standard
options_why: A policy would be more general, like “we protect our computers”.
A guideline does not make anything mandatory.
A procedure says how to do something, not what is required.
cards.answer: A standard
cards.explanation: An exact requirement that can be checked on each computer is a standard.

cards.question: Pizza Express wants to show a new worker how to report a strange email, step by step. Which document fits?
options: A policy
A procedure
A standard
A guideline
options_why: A policy says why. It does not give steps.
A standard says what is required, not how to do it.
A guideline gives optional tips, not exact steps.
cards.answer: A procedure
cards.explanation: Steps in order are a procedure.

cards.question: Pizza Express wants to give workers a few optional tips on strong passwords. Which document fits?
options: A standard
A policy
A guideline
A procedure
options_why: A standard is required. These tips are optional.
A policy is a formal text of principles.
A procedure gives exact steps.
cards.answer: A guideline
cards.explanation: Optional tips are a guideline.

cards.question: Which sentence about backups is a procedure?
options: Open the tool, pick the date, click Restore
A backup is made every night
The company's data must be able to come back
We recommend keeping a copy in another building
options_why: This is an exact requirement, so it is a standard.
This is a broad principle, so it is a policy.
This is a tip, so it is a guideline.
cards.answer: Open the tool, pick the date, click Restore
cards.explanation: Actions in order are a procedure.

cards.question: Which document is the LEAST strict?
options: The guideline
The policy
The standard
The procedure
options_why: A policy is a formal text that the company must follow.
A standard must be followed and enforced.
A procedure gives the exact steps to follow.
cards.answer: The guideline
cards.explanation: A guideline is a recommendation, so it is the least strict.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Develop, Document, and Implement Security Policy, Standards, Procedures, and Guidelines”.

cards.question: A company has a good policy, but workers do not know how to apply it. Which document would help MOST?
options: A second copy of the same policy
A policy with fewer words
Procedures that show the steps
A tip list that nobody must follow
options_why: The workers already have the goal. They need the steps.
A shorter goal does not show how to act.
Optional tips do not make sure that everyone acts in the same way.
cards.answer: Procedures that show the steps
cards.explanation: Procedures tell you how to implement your policies.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Develop, Document, and Implement Security Policy, Standards, Procedures, and Guidelines”.

cards.question: Which document sets the minimum security level for a computer or a server?
options: A policy
A baseline
A guideline
A procedure
